issue.title: [Bug]: GitLab inline comments on unchanged diff lines omit their old position
issue.author: Afloat16
issue.body:
### Where were you using Orca?

Other

### Operating system

Linux

### Remote host operating system

None

### Orca version

Source checkout at 2194f552640e2afe07f9507f885251045c05c9e8

### Details

The GitLab merge-request Files tab allows an inline comment on a context line, but Orca's request contains only `position[new_line]`. GitLab requires both new and old coordinates for unchanged lines. When earlier changes shift the line numbers, the old coordinate is different.

**Reproduction**

1. Open a GitLab merge request whose file includes this unified diff:

```diff
@@ -1,7 +1,6 @@
 one
-remove-a
-remove-b
 context-after-delete
-old
+replacement-a
+replacement-b
 context-after-replace
 last
```

2. In the MR's Files tab, select the changed file, enter line `2`, write a comment and submit. Repeat for line `5`.
3. The existing submit action sends only `new_line=2` or `new_line=5`. The correct positions are `old_line=4,new_line=2` and `old_line=6,new_line=5`.
4. As an ordinary-input control, submit on added line `3`; that request should continue to omit `old_line`.

**Observed before:** a fixture enforcing GitLab's documented contract rejects both context comments; the production dialog action appends no comment. The added-line control succeeds.

**Expected:** context comments include both correct coordinates; added-line comments include only the new coordinate.

**Evidence and limits:** the fixture uses a real `git diff --no-index` output and calls the actual submit hook, runtime RPC schema and `addMRInlineComment` mutation. The baseline has 2 failing context cases and 1 passing added-line control; the fix passes all 3. The only simulated boundary is external provider execution, plus presentation dependencies used to mount the hook. This is not a live GitLab server or rendered desktop capture.

GitLab's contract: https://docs.gitlab.com/api/discussions/#create-a-new-thread-in-the-merge-request-diff

Related work #50688 preserves ranges while reading discussions; this defect is the position submitted when creating a single-line discussion.

pr.title: fix(gitlab): include old positions when commenting on context lines
pr.author: Afloat16
pr.head: b561366bf77411f6e7056eb2cac9b2b3bf6082c0
pr.body:
## ELI5

A comment on an unchanged line in a GitLab merge-request diff needs two line numbers: its position before the change and after it. Orca only sent the second one. This supplies the missing first number from the diff already shown in the Files tab.

## What Changed

- The existing Files comment action finds the old coordinate only for a real context row within a declared diff hunk.
- An optional `oldLine` crosses the existing input type and runtime RPC schema.
- The current discussion POST includes `position[old_line]` when that coordinate exists. Added and unmapped lines receive no invented old coordinate.

Before, new line 2 in the reproduction was submitted without its old line 4 and failed the provider contract. After, the same action submits the pair `old_line=4,new_line=2` and accepts the created comment.

## Why

GitLab requires both coordinates for context comments. Additions and deletions can shift their relationship, so copying the new number into the old field would attach a wrong position. The Files reply already contains the per-file diff; using it avoids another provider read.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #50736

## Visual Proof

The interaction changes: context-line comments that previously failed can complete and appear in the current MR conversation. The form layout is unchanged. No rendered Electron before/after screenshot or video was captured; the visual-proof checkbox remains unchecked.

The following is recorded production-request evidence from the local reproduction, not a desktop screenshot:

| Input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Context after two deleted rows | `new_line=2`; rejected, no appended comment | `old_line=4,new_line=2`; comment appended |
| Context after replacement inserts | `new_line=5`; rejected, no appended comment | `old_line=6,new_line=5`; comment appended |
| Added line | `new_line=3`; accepted | `new_line=3`; accepted |

## Testing

- [x] I exercised the production-entry reproduction locally as described below
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below
- [x] The regression checks the actual parser's fixed mapping and avoids the [test anti-patterns](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/main/docs/agents-md-refs/test-antipatterns.md)

**Behavior baseline:** a real Git-generated diff was passed through the existing React submit hook, real RPC schema and real main-process mutation. The external `glab` boundary enforces GitLab's documented position contract. On 2194f552640e2afe07f9507f885251045c05c9e8, both context cases failed with no appended comment; the ordinary added-line case passed. With the fix, all three passed.

**Committed regression:** one parser invariant covers distinct old/new coordinates, separated hunks, omitted counts, all-added/all-deleted hunks, exhausted ranges and malformed rows. It passed. This new parser did not exist on main: an import failure from deleting it is not counted as evidence of the original bug. The behavior baseline above is separate from this new parser test. The local hook/RPC reproduction is not committed as a wiring/UI unit test.

```sh
ORCA_BACKGROUND_LAUNCH=1 node config/scripts/test-runtime/execution-policy/run-vitest.mjs run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/shared/gitlab/mr-inline-comment-position.test.ts --maxWorkers=2
```

Linux source-level validation used the installed repository runner. Scoped formatting and lint passed on all six files, and the diff check emitted no whitespace diagnostics. No live GitLab account, macOS, Windows, SSH or rendered Electron session was exercised.

Current candidate `b561366bf77411f6e7056eb2cac9b2b3bf6082c0` passed the [complete required `pnpm check:changed` gate in exact-source fork CI](https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/actions/runs/45974662879/job/140423292471). The job verified the exact candidate and base `2194f552640e2afe07f9507f885251045c05c9e8`, and confirmed that validation left tracked sources unchanged.

## Performance

One scan of the already-loaded file diff when the user submits an inline comment. The parser retains counters and one current row, and stops when it finds the requested context row. No extra API request, Git process, polling, disk write or render-time scan is added.

## Risk

**Level:** Low

The main risk is supplying a wrong old coordinate after additions or deletions. The parser advances old and new counters independently and returns an old number only for a prefixed context row inside the declared ranges. It does not infer an old number for additions, missing diffs or unmapped lines. It validates the consumed prefix; it does not promise whole-document validation after the selected row.

`oldLine` is optional, so old callers remain valid. An older paired runtime strips the unknown field and retains the old context-comment limitation: update both the client and runtime for the fix to take effect. There is no migration. A plain revert restores the previous behavior; it does not delete comments already posted to GitLab.

## AI Disclosure

Core contribution owner: @Afloat16. Required tooling disclosure: GPT-6 Astra Pro was used for implementation and review.

## Review

Checked the actual MR Files form, desktop IPC and runtime RPC routes, and GitLab's documented request contract. Independent read-only review found no concrete blocker. This changes portable string parsing and an existing request field; it adds no shell command or platform-specific path behavior. Deleted-side commenting remains outside this fix.

## Agent skill upstream boundary

- [x] Not applicable: this change copies or mechanically translates no upstream skill-installer source, tests, fixtures, registry entries, path tables, comments or documentation.

## Notes

Official contract: https://docs.gitlab.com/api/discussions/#create-a-new-thread-in-the-merge-request-diff

Historical deduplication covered all 71 prior Afloat16 Orca PRs, the current batch of 50 and focused repository-wide PR/commit searches. #50688 concerns reading multiline discussion ranges; #12133 and #19505 concern diff line counts. None implements this submitted context-coordinate fix.
